method: After freezing the decision and canonical pair, returned to the adopted 2026–2027 regulations, appendix, current programme tables and the project guidance. Recomputed credit groups and separately reconsidered level, elective and research entry rules. Rechecked current workbook content and the final record references.
findings: The 180 EC full-time degree comprises a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling. The OER lists 75 EC of compulsory courses: seven 7.5 EC first-year courses plus 15 EC Onderzoeksmethoden and 7.5 EC Bio-informatica. The other 60 EC include the 7.5 EC first-year biomedical elective, at least five 7.5 EC major-list courses including Moleculaire Biologie van de Cel, and the standard 15 EC project. The 22.5 EC Plus option replaces the standard project and requires balancing the degree within the applicable rules. The review retains restricted choice and does not assume a named minor or route. At least 75 major EC must be at level 2 or 3, including 30 EC at level 3. The full degree must include 45 EC at level 3. At least 15 profiling EC must be at level 2 or 3, subject to entry and exclusions, and the examination board can reduce overlapping credit.

The standard binding study-advice threshold and second-year entry threshold are 45 first-year EC. The standard Researchproject requires 150 EC, while Plus requires 135 EC, with the separate honours exceptions in the OER. The student project instructions also describe two followed courses awaiting results and consultation in other circumstances. Clinical Immunology requires Infection & Immunity. Molecular Mechanisms of Cancer requires Genoom and Moleculaire Biologie van de Cel, and Advanced Bioinformatics requires Genoom. Registration periods, timeslots, capacity and specified selection apply. The standard project typically runs in period four and includes literature study, practical research or an experiment, an English thesis and an integrity module. The supervisor and a second reviewer assess the final work and the examiner records the result. Plus adds practical research time.

The research project is required as a culmination, even though the standard 15 EC and expanded 22.5 EC project sit in major choice under the OER. The first-year elective and restricted later choices are retained without assuming student selections. Molecular Cell Biology is shown explicitly because it is required within the restricted list. Utrecht Genoom includes genetic mechanisms, so the stronger UCR alignment is Molecular Pathology & Genetics, while biochemistry aligns to Moleculen. Utrecht’s dedicated tumour project has no scheduled equivalent. The UCR advanced methods course supports systematic review and evidence appraisal and cannot substitute for Utrecht’s thesis. The UCR programmes use actual shared biomedical content and distinct computing or behavioural emphasis, and all three schedules pass current offerings and prerequisites.
